stem:
Tara looks at the diagram. Parallel lines $m$ and $n$ are cut by transversal $t$. One same-side interior angle is marked $75^{\circ}$.

Which claim correctly gives the other same-side interior angle?

options.text: Call the answer the transversal $t$, and stop.
The other same-side interior angle is $75^{\circ}$, because those angles are equal.
The other same-side interior angle is $105^{\circ}$, because same-side interior angles on parallel lines add to $180^{\circ}$.
The other same-side interior angle is $150^{\circ}$, from doubling $75^{\circ}$.

teacher.key_rationale: Same-side interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary: 180−75=105. Naming the transversal, treating them as equal, or doubling 75 miss that.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as parallel lines m and n cut by transversal t with one same-side interior angle 75°.
